item.research_question: Can high-entropy doping improve the cycling performance and stability of layered Ni-rich oxide cathodes in lithium-ion batteries?
item.material_system: Layered Ni-rich oxide cathodes, such as LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2 (NCM-811) and LiNi0.5Co0.3Mn0.2O2 (NCM-532), with high-entropy doping
item.test_conditions: Cycling at C/10 rate, C/3 rate, and 1C rate, with potential ranges of 2.5 to 4.4 V, 2.7 to 4.5 V, and 2.8 to 4.3 V versus Li+/Li
key_findings: HE-LNMO exhibited a well-defined layered structure with uniformly distributed dopants
HE-LNMO showed minor volume variations of about 0.3% during battery operation
HE-LNMO delivered a capacity retention of 98.5% after 100 cycles
HE-N50 outperformed NCM-532 after 20 cycles at C/3 rate
HE-N50 delivered a high specific energy of 642 Wh/kg with 95% capacity retention after 100 cycles
HE-N50 showed much superior stability, retaining almost 95% of the initial capacity after 1,000 cycles at 1C rate
HE-N50 underwent phase transformation from layered to ordered spinel without any visible cracking upon heating at 350 °C for 30 min
item.mechanism: The "cocktail effects" from multiple constituents, which lead to synergistic effects and improved performance, such as reduced strain accumulation and immobilization of oxygen vacancies
item.future_work: Exploring more nuanced factors in element selection, such as the impact of electronegativity, and integrating high-entropy doping strategies with other approaches, such as single-crystal synthesis
quotes: the key to improved performance lies in the synergistic effect of all constituents
compositionally complex doping or substitution strategies may pave the way toward the development of next-generation electrode materials

records.text: Paper card. Question: Can high-entropy doping improve the cycling performance and stability of layered Ni-rich oxide cathodes in lithium-ion batteries?. System: Layered Ni-rich oxide cathodes, such as LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2 (NCM-811) and LiNi0.5Co0.3Mn0.2O2 (NCM-532), with high-entropy doping. Test conditions: Cycling at C/10 rate, C/3 rate, and 1C rate, with potential ranges of 2.5 to 4.4 V, 2.7 to 4.5 V, and 2.8 to 4.3 V versus Li+/Li. Findings: HE-LNMO exhibited a well-defined layered structure with uniformly distributed dopants; HE-LNMO showed minor volume variations of about 0.3% during battery operation; HE-LNMO delivered a capacity retention of 98.5% after 100 cycles; HE-N50 outperformed NCM-532 after 20 cycles at C/3 rate; HE-N50 delivered a high specific energy of 642 Wh/kg with 95% capacity retention after 100 cycles; HE-N50 showed much superior stability, retaining almost 95% of the initial capacity after 1,000 cycles at 1C rate; HE-N50 underwent phase transformation from layered to ordered spinel without any visible cracking upon heating at 350 °C for 30 min. Mechanism: The "cocktail effects" from multiple constituents, which lead to synergistic effects and improved performance, such as reduced strain accumulation and immobilization of oxygen vacancies. Future work: Exploring more nuanced factors in element selection, such as the impact of electronegativity, and integrating high-entropy doping strategies with other approaches, such as single-crystal synthesis. Quote: "introducing "cocktail effects" from multiple constituents"
